query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled amount of rhenium (Re) to the equiatomic NbMoTaW alloy (to form, for example, a Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 composition) will improve room-temperature ductility by refining the grain structure and producing nanoscale amorphous films along grain boundaries that facilitate dislocation motion, while maintaining the inherent high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance of the original alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, single-phase, equiatomic refractory high-entropy NbMoTaW alloy (typically produced by magnetron sputtering to yield a columnar nanocrystalline BCC microstructure).
generation.intervention: Incorporation of approximately 20 atomic percent Re into the composition (forming NbMoTaWRe) during processing.
generation.conditions: Films produced via magnetron sputtering at room temperature under controlled pressure; mechanical testing performed at room temperature for ductility, at 1600 °C for high-temperature performance, and irradiation by 120 keV He²⁺ implantation (fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm², dose rate circa 1 × 10^13 ions/cm²/s) to assess irradiation resistance.
generation.structural_mediator: Re addition is expected to refine the grain size, increase overall grain-boundary density, introduce greater lattice distortion and excess free volume, and promote the formation of several-nanometer-wide amorphous intergranular films.
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure and amorphous grain-boundary films act as effective defect-sink sites that both enhance plasticity at room temperature (by supporting enhanced dislocation mobility and mitigating grain-boundary embrittlement) and suppress irradiation-induced damage such as He-bubble coalescence. These features are also anticipated to preserve the high-temperature mechanical performance as they do not compromise the inherent BCC strength of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Re-free NbMoTaW baseline, the NbMoTaWRe alloy is predicted to show improved room-temperature ductility (i.e., increased strain to failure and enhanced plastic deformation) without a significant reduction in high-temperature mechanical strength at 1600 °C or its irradiation resistance (evidenced by reduced He-bubble agglomeration and irradiation-induced hardening).
generation.baseline: The baseline is the performance of equiatomic Re-free NbMoTaW, which, while exhibiting excellent high-temperature strength and predicted irradiation resistance, shows very poor room-temperature ductility.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for magnetron-sputtered NbMoTaW-based films maintaining a single-phase BCC structure under the specified processing, mechanical testing, and irradiation conditions. Its validity beyond these specific processing routes, microstructural features, or compositional ranges remains to be established.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism for improved ductility via grain refinement and amorphous boundary formation is supported by prior observations of Re addition effects in similar systems, the quantitative improvement in room-temperature ductility and the balance of high-temperature and irradiation performance may vary with processing conditions and scaling to bulk materials.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of magnetron-sputtered films: one set of equiatomic NbMoTaW and another set of NbMoTaW with ~20 at.% Re, ensuring a single-phase BCC structure in each. Characterize the microstructure via TEM and XRD to confirm grain refinement and the existence of amorphous intergranular films in the Re-containing alloy. Then, perform room-temperature mechanical testing (e.g., nanoindentation and in situ micropillar compression) to determine ductility, high-temperature mechanical testing at 1600 °C, and He irradiation experiments using 120 keV He²⁺ (with the described fluence and dose rate). Post-irradiation, use TEM to evaluate the distribution and size of He bubbles and nanoindentation to assess irradiation-induced hardening.
measurements: Grain size and identification of amorphous boundary films (TEM, XRD)
Room-temperature plastic deformation characteristics (strain to failure, ductility via micropillar compression)
Irradiation effects via He-bubble morphology and nanoindentation hardness measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Re-containing NbMoTaWRe samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in room-temperature ductility relative to the Re-free NbMoTaW baseline, or if there is a notable degradation in high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance (e.g., similar or worse He-bubble segregation and hardening), then the hypothesis must be rejected.
